notes: Appendix A of RFC 7396 is a fifteen-row table of original document, patch, and result, transcribed here in order as merge-a01 through merge-a15. The cases after it come from the pseudocode in section 2 and cover the branches the table exercises only once. Merge patch has no failure mode of its own, so every merge case expects success; the interesting behaviour is which of the target and the patch wins.

field_guide.kind: merge for a case that applies a patch, diff for a case that computes one.
field_guide.original: merge cases: the target document the patch is applied to.
field_guide.patch: merge cases: the merge patch. A null here is a deletion request, not an absent field.
field_guide.result: merge cases: the document the merge must produce. Compared member-order-insensitively.
field_guide.source: diff cases: the document to transform from.
field_guide.target: diff cases: the document to transform to.
field_guide.expected_patch: diff cases: the merge patch a conforming generator produces. A generator may legitimately produce a different but equivalent patch, so the runner also checks the round trip, that applying the generated patch to source yields target.
field_guide.expect: apply for every case in this corpus. Kept for symmetry with the other two catalogs.

cases.title: A.1 A patch member replaces the same member in the target
A.2 A patch member not in the target is added
A.3 A null in the patch deletes the member
A.4 Deleting one member leaves the others
A.5 A scalar in the patch replaces an array in the target
A.6 An array in the patch replaces a scalar in the target
A.7 Objects merge recursively, and a nested null deletes
cases.notes: Deleting a member that was never there is a no-op, not an error.

cases.title: A.8 Arrays are replaced wholesale, never merged element-wise
cases.notes: This is the deliberate limitation of merge patch: there is no way to edit one element of an array.

cases.title: A.9 A top-level array patch replaces a top-level array target
A.10 A top-level array patch replaces an object target
A.11 A top-level null patch replaces the whole document with null
cases.notes: null only means delete when it is the value of a member inside an object patch. At the top level it is an ordinary replacement value.

cases.title: A.12 A top-level string patch replaces the whole document
A.13 A null already in the target is left alone
cases.notes: Only a null in the patch means delete. An implementation that prunes nulls from its output drops /e here.

cases.title: A.14 An object patch replaces an array target before merging
cases.notes: The array target is discarded and replaced by an empty object, so the deletion of /c has nothing to delete and is a no-op.

cases.title: A.15 Deleting inside an object the patch itself created
cases.notes: The nested objects are created even though every leaf in the patch is a deletion, so the result keeps an empty /a/bb.

cases.title: A non-object patch replaces the target wholesale
cases.paragraph: If the provided merge patch is not an Object, the result of applying it is to replace the entire target with the entire patch.
cases.notes: A number is the plainest form of the non-object branch, and nothing about the target is consulted.

cases.title: An object patch on an array target starts from an empty object
cases.paragraph: if Target is not an Object: Target = {} # Ignore the contents and set it to an empty Object
cases.notes: The target's elements are discarded rather than merged in under numeric keys.

cases.title: A nested null deletes one leaf and leaves its siblings
cases.paragraph: if Value is null: if Name exists in Target: remove the Name/Value pair from Target
cases.notes: The recursion must rebuild /a/b in place rather than replacing it with the patch's own sub-object.

cases.title: A generated patch adds the new member and nulls the dropped one
cases.paragraph: This design means that merge patch documents are suitable for describing modifications to JSON documents that primarily use objects for their structure and do not make use of explicit null values.
cases.notes: The unchanged member /a must not appear in the patch.

cases.title: A generated patch recurses rather than replacing a whole sub-object
cases.notes: Emitting the whole new /a would also be correct on application, but it is larger and loses the point of a merge patch.

cases.title: A generated patch emits a changed array in full
cases.notes: Arrays have no partial representation in merge patch, so the only available description is the whole new array.
